newsitem.title: GREECE: RALLYING-KANKKUNEN LEADS IN ACROPOLIS AS MAKINEN HITS TROUBLE.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-KANKKUNEN LEADS IN ACROPOLIS AS MAKINEN HITS TROUBLE.

text.p: Finland's Juha Kankkunen maintained his overnight lead of the Acropolis Rally on Monday but he was having to work hard on the tough gravel stages to fight off an inspired challenge by Briton Richard Burns in the Mitsubishi.

Kankkunen, who drives for Ford, had started the day with a lead of 27 seconds over Burns, but the gap was reduced by 10 seconds as the Briton put in a charge and set the joint fastest time with Ford's Carlos Sainz on the 10th stage.
But on the 11th stage, Kankkunen managed to extend his advantage by another six seconds to leave himself a 23 seconds advantage as the teams headed back towards the overnight halt of Kamena Vourla.
The pace of the two front-runners saw them pull clear of their nearest rivals, with third place Spaniard Carlos Sainz in the Ford more than one minute behind Kankkunen.

World championship leader Tommi Makinen, who started the day with the same time as Mitsubishi team-mate Burns, broke a driveshaft in an accident on stage eight and was down in fourth place at the end of the 11th stage, almost five minutes behind Kankkunen.
The rough gravel stages to the north of Kamena Vourla also claimed more victims on Monday following the first day retirement of championship front-runner Briton Colin McRae.
His Subaru team-mate, Swede Kenneth Eriksson, retired at the end of the opening stage of the day when he damaged his steering after landing off a steep jump.

"Everything was going fine and I had no concerns," explained Eriksson, who had been running in 14th position after a roll on the opening day. "We were going through a fast left-hander and then onto a straight over a jump.

"When we landed I felt something was wrong with the steering so we stopped and checked and saw that the track rod end had bent. We managed to fix it so we could continue, but eventually the strain on it was too much and it broke."

That eighth stage had to be cancelled later on when the Ford car of Monaco's Jean-Pierre Richelmi rolled out of the event and burst into flames. Although the crew were unhurt in the incident, officials had to suspend the stage so the car could be cleared.
The incident also led to confusion on the following stage at Makrirahi when spectators accidentally blocked the stage after a large gap between the 15th and 16th cars saw them wander onto the road.
